answer: Each agent binds identity to one limestone core from a single island outcrop, fitted with a copper electrode mesh registered on-chain. Each epoch a secret current schedule is revealed late; the agent must drive it through the mesh in a tight window and publish nonce-signed impedance traces of that core's unique karst drainage paths. Peer attestors replay the schedule on the deposited specimen and countersign only matching traces. Clones cannot fake the pore geometry; fabricating a second wired rock is costly and fails a later cross-probe, so duplicates are slashed.
